items.title: feat(packages/excalidraw): replace the export functions with `exportScene`

labels.name: s-package
labels.description: scope: package (related to packages/* API, not necessarily user facing)

items.body:
An export API rewrite. API may slightly break in the coming days/weeks yet.

---

Rewrites the export API of `@excalidraw/excalidraw` and `@excalidraw/utils`. **Breaking** — the CHANGELOG has a migration table.

- `exportToCanvas` / `exportToBlob` / `exportToSvg` → `exportScene({ type: "canvas" | "png" | "jpeg" | "svg", data, config })`, with the return type following `type`. `exportToClipboard` stays.
- Every rendering option is explicit `config` (`theme`, `canvasBackgroundColor`, `padding`, `scale`, `frames`, `embedScene`, sizing, …). `data` is `{ elements, appState?, files? }`, and only the scene settings a `.excalidraw` file stores are read from `appState`, so editor state can't leak into an export.
- Sizing: `width`/`height` (a missing one follows the aspect ratio) with `fit`/`position`, `maxWidthOrHeight`, `widthOrHeight`, an `x`/`y` region (cropped), and `scale` as a number or `(width, height) => number`. The options are mutually exclusive in the types. `getDimensions` is removed.
- `config.environment` (`createCanvas`, `loadFonts`) for non-browser hosts.
- Unchanged: elements are restored and deleted ones dropped (#11470), embeds and the json clipboard copy restored elements (#12060), default padding 10.
- Fixes: dark exports use the editor's frame-name color; canvas sizes are rounded instead of truncated, and at least 1px.
- `dev-docs` and the utils README still describe the stable API.

Notes:
- Collides with #11997: its canvas/SVG host options should become `config.environment` members once this lands.
- Supersedes #6086 and #5825.

Tested: typecheck and the full suite (142 files, 2493 tests); smoke-tested every output type, the export dialog and frame-export clipping in Chrome.

Claude Opus 5.5 (xhigh)

items.title: fix(editor): frame membership, clipping and cut fixes
items.body:
- **Snapped frames take elements in**: a new or resized frame matching an element's (or group's) edges now contains it. Frame membership measures elements by their outline (not stroke) and allows a tiny tolerance (`PRECISION`) for the float noise snapping leaves.
- **Frames always clip their children**: a child sitting just inside the frame was left unclipped and its stroke bled out. Children are now clipped like in SVG exports, without the per-child geometry check (cheaper render). Children being dragged are still checked like the drop will be, so one dragged out stays visible.
- **Cut takes frame children along**: cutting a frame (or frame + children) removes its children too — they're on the clipboard with it. Delete still leaves them.

Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context), effort: medium

items.title: feat(editor): `w` to wrap/unwrap selection
items.body:
`w` picks the wrap/unwrap that fits the selection, preferring containers over frames:

1. text + empty container → binds the text
2. texts (+ any labeled containers) → wraps each text in a container
3. labeled containers → unwraps the texts and removes the containers (any type, incl. arrows/sticky notes); arrows bound to a container move onto its text
4. a frame (+ its children), or all of a frame's children → removes the frame
5. anything else without a frame → wraps it in a frame

Notes:
- after (3), the next `w` on the untouched selection brings back the same containers (not new rectangles), at wherever the text was moved, with their arrows; connecting arrows stay anchored and their label returns to them
- "Wrap selection in frame" (context menu): frames an image (and what lies on it) with 0 padding; with all of a frame's children selected it reads "Remove frame" and removes it
- "Unbind text" keeps the text selected along with its container
- added to the help dialog and command palette

Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context), effort: medium

items.title: feat(editor): crop editor modifiers as resizing, and double-click a handle to uncrop
items.body:
Crop editor:

- **shift-click** on the image being cropped keeps the crop editor open (it toggled the image out of the selection, which ended cropping)
- **shift-drag** of the image within its crop locks it to one axis, as dragging elements does
- **alt-drag** a crop handle crops from the center, as far as the image reaches on the nearer side
- handles crop as resizing resizes: from the drag's start, so pressing or releasing **alt**/**shift** mid-drag applies right away; with shift, a corner follows the axis that grows most (relatively), not the one moved most in pixels
- **double-click** a crop handle uncrops its side (a corner: its two sides); with **alt**, the opposite side(s) too, so alt+double-click on a corner uncrops the whole image

Fixes:

- clicking a crop handle without moving no longer exits the crop editor
- no invisible rotation handle in the crop editor: pressing where it would be hit it, and dragging it cropped the image; a press there now leaves the editor, as any click outside
- the image no longer shifts by a pixel within the crop while cropping (the cropped bitmap snapped to whole pixels by its own corner, the faded uncropped one by its own); within the crop, the editor now draws the uncropped bitmap at full opacity, clipped
- arrows bound to the image follow the sides uncropped by a double-click

Code:

- `cropElement` rebuilt on resize's sizing (`getNextSingleWidthAndHeightFromPointer`), clamped to the image, applied through `cropElementToBounds`; `cropElement.ts` 628 → 359 lines
- `cropElement` takes the element at the drag's start and `{ shouldMaintainAspectRatio, shouldResizeFromCenter }` instead of a width aspect ratio: breaking for `@excalidraw/element` consumers (E+ doesn't use it)
- new `@excalidraw/element` export: `uncropElementSides`
- `maybeHandleResize` hands off to `maybeHandleCrop` in the crop editor, so modifier keys re-crop as they re-resize
- dragging the image within its crop applies the offset's change since the previous move (`pointerDownState.drag.lastOffset`), so it still moves back right away after being dragged past its edge; drops `App.previousPointerMoveCoords`
- alt in the crop editor: no alt-drag threshold, and alt double-clicks aren't ignored, since alt-clicks don't cycle the selection there

Claude Opus 5.5 (1M), xhigh effort

items.title: refactor(editor): app.selection, and the rest of the selection tool out of App
items.body:
- `app.selection` ([App.selection.ts](packages/excalidraw/components/App.selection.ts)): `select` / `add` / `remove` / `clear`, taking elements or ids, one or many — one place for the selection's rules

  - what hangs on the selection follows it: the link popup, cropping, an active embed, and text editing (submitted after the current event)
  - `captureUpdate` (as `updateScene`'s) and `deep` (the elements themselves, editing their shared group — Ctrl+click goes through it)
  - pure `getSelectionState{For,Adding,Removing}Elements` for callers that need the next state rather than a `setState` (duplication, actions); `getSelectionStateForElements` and `selectGroupsForSelectedElements` move there from `@excalidraw/element` (editor state, used by the editor only)
  - replaces `App.deselectElements` and the inline copies in the selection tool, the lasso and the context menu
- `AppSelectionTool`: dragging the selection, box selection and the drag end's frame membership move out of App (pure moves, verified mechanically); one check for the transform handle under the pointer, shared by the hover cursor and pointer down
- Fixes along the way
  - shift-click deselecting a group put element ids into `selectedGroupIds`, dropping the other selected groups
  - the link popup was left as is by programmatic selection, so `select()` showed it only if a previous selection had
  - an arrow selected with its group (alt-click cycling, a second click) got its own line editor, so dragging from its point reshaped it alone
  - adding within an edited group containing a frame could deselect as if that frame were selected

  - pointer down ignored the element link selector for transform handles, unlike the hover cursor

items.title: feat(editor): autoplay Google Drive videos when the embed is activated
items.body:
Clicking a Google Drive video embed now plays it. Before, the first click only activated the embed and a second click was needed (in view mode too).

https://excalidraw-git-dwelle-gdrive-autoplay-excalidraw.vercel.app/#json=j7610j5jjBToYDm4ABUQn,2IoNleVuYVJsXnyS9PFKiQ

- **Why a reload:** Drive's player has no postMessage API like YouTube/Vimeo. It nests a blank YouTube player that only accepts commands from `drive.google.com`. Its `/preview` page does honor `autoplay=1` (undocumented), so the first activation reloads the embed with it. If Drive drops the param, it falls back to today's behavior.
- **No history entry:** the reload uses `contentWindow.location.replace` because setting `src` adds a session-history entry, so Back would step back inside the embed.
- **Once per iframe:** re-activating doesn't reload and restart the video. A remounted iframe (e.g. undo of a delete) doesn't autoplay on mount.
- **Play only:** unlike YouTube, there's no play/pause toggle on re-activation, because Drive gives us no player state.
- Test: first activation reloads with `autoplay=1`, re-activation doesn't. It fails with either the `replace` or the once-only change reverted.

Claude Opus 5.5 (1M), xhigh effort

items.title: refactor(editor): move the clipboard out of App into AppClipboard (app.clipboard)
items.body:
Pure move of the clipboard handling out of `App.tsx` (13,478 → 12,942 lines) into `App.clipboard.ts` / `AppClipboard` (`app.clipboard`). Follows #12195.

**`AppClipboard` holds**
- `onCut` and `onCopy`: the document's cut and copy events, handled through their actions
- `pasteFromClipboard`: the paste event, parsed, and handed to a host's `onPaste` first
- `insertClipboardContent`: inserts the pasted data as whatever it is (images or SVG code, elements, Mermaid, embeddable URLs, a spreadsheet as a chart, mixed content, or text), with `addElementsFromMixedContentPaste` and `addTextFromPaste`
- the plain-paste flags, still module-level. Ctrl/Cmd+V's marking of a plain paste, and its reset, are App's former lines behind `onPasteShortcut` / `clearPlainPaste`.

**Stays in `App`**
- `addElementsFromPasteOrLibrary` and `insertImages`, which drop, the library and text-to-diagram also use. `insertImages` is now public.
- `onIframeSrcCopy`, which is magic-frame code.

**Beyond the move**
- Callers go through `app.clipboard`, with no delegate left on `App`. `AppClassProperties` exposes `clipboard`, as it does `textTool`, instead of `pasteFromClipboard`.
- `this.` → `this.app.` for what stays on `App`, `onCut`/`onCopy` are now public, and the container ref comes in as a dependency. The moved code was checked mechanically: it's identical to the removed code, modulo those rewrites, whitespace and trailing commas.

**Tests**
- Coverage of the moved code was 80% of lines, and `addElementsFromMixedContentPaste` never ran.
- New tests: copy and cut through the document's events (the path Ctrl/Cmd+C and X take), a host's `onPaste` returning `false`, a spreadsheet paste opening the charts dialog, and mixed-content text pasted with the image tool off.
- Now all functions run, and 90% of lines. What's left is mostly the image-URL fetch inside mixed content, plus error and phone-only branches.

items.title: feat(editor): wrap text at 800 and keep it clear of the side panels
items.body:
Follow-up to #12175, which made a typed text stop growing at the view's width. On large screens, that still meant lines of 2000+px.

**Wrap width**
- Typed and pasted text now wraps at `TEXT_MAX_WRAP_WIDTH` (800, in scene units, at any zoom). Paste used to wrap at half the view.
- Both also stay within the canvas between the side panels:
  - the docked sidebar, as before
  - the full styles panel (desktop). When pasting with nothing selected, its room is reserved, since it only appears once the text is selected.
  - the stats panel, but only for a text beside it. It covers just the top of the right edge, so a text below it can run past it.

**Paste**
- A wrapped paste is moved into view instead of scrolling the canvas.
- With the stats panel open, the paste is rendered selected first (`flushSync`, before the undo capture), because the panel grows to show the selection's properties. The panels are then measured at their real sizes, and the text is laid out again if needed, keeping the same ids. It stays one undo step.

**Typing**
- The canvas pans when the caret goes under the stats or styles panel, but only then; a text beside or below a panel stays put. Before, it only followed the caret past the viewport's edge or behind the docked sidebar.
- In lines with RTL characters, the caret's position comes from the browser's bidi layout, in the paragraph's own direction. The editor's `dir="auto"` makes it `unicode-bidi: plaintext`.

**Worth a look**
- The stats panel is now marked `data-viewport-ui="side"`, so zoom to fit, scroll to content, search and a host's `setViewport` UI offsets also keep clear of it while it's open.
- New: `TEXT_MAX_WRAP_WIDTH` and `hasRTLChars` in `@excalidraw/common`, and `AppViewport.getSideInsets(names, { reserve })` and `getSideUIRect(name)`.

Claude Opus 5.5 (1M), xhigh effort

items.title: feat(editor): auto increment numbers/lists on duplicate
items.body:
When duplicating (Ctrl+D, alt-drag) a text or a label (shape, arrow, sticky note) that starts with a list marker, the marker is advanced: `1. foo` → `2. foo`.

**Markers** (leading whitespace ignored, must be followed by whitespace or the end of the text)
- numbers: `1.` `1)` `(1)` `[1]`, and lone numbers (`1`); zero padding is kept (`09.` → `10.`); up to `42`
- letters: `a.` `a)` `(a)` (any case), from `a` to `h` → up to `i`
- roman numerals, from `i` up: `i.` → `ii.`, `(IV)` → `(V)`; up to `xcix`
- not markers: `[a]`, `1.5`, `e.g.`, other letters (`j.`), mixed case (`Ii.`)

**Left as is**
- a whole list (another line starts with a marker of the same style)
- list items duplicated along with anything else (other texts or elements); a label goes with its container
- several list items with text (`1. foo` `2. bar`)
- markers past their limit

**Multiple items** (just markers) continue from the highest, per marker style: `1.` `3.` `5.` → `6.` `7.` `8.`

**Undo**: the increment is a separate undo step (first undo reverts the marker, second removes the duplicate).

**Alt-drag**: the new marker shows from the start of the drag. On drop, a single list item with text after its marker is edited with that text selected (`2. |foo|`); not for interrupted drags.

Opus 5.5 (1M context), xhigh

items.title: fix(editor): follow-ups to zen mode polish & delayed tooltips

items.title: feat(editor): add showHints to command palette
items.body:
Follow-up to #12165.

`showHints` is the only item in the Preferences submenu that flips `appState` directly instead of going through an action:

```tsx
// DefaultItems.tsx, before
setAppState({ showHints: !appState.showHints });
```

while every sibling (`objectsSnapMode`, `arrowBinding`, `midpointSnapping`, `gridMode`, `zenMode`, `viewMode`, `stats`) calls `actionManager.executeAction(...)`. That left it without anything the action system provides:

- no command palette entry — `CommandPalette` enumerates `actionManager.actions.*`, so a non-action can't appear there at all
- no `trackEvent`
- no `viewMode` declaration

There was also no behavioural test coverage for the preference, only incidental snapshot entries, and no CHANGELOG entry for the new public `appState.showHints` field.

## Changes

- add `actionToggleShowHints`, modelled on `actionToggleMidpointSnapping`. `viewMode: false`, since `HintViewer` lives inside the toolbar `Island`, which view mode hides entirely
- register `"showHints"` in `ActionName` and export the action from `actions/index.ts`
- `PreferencesToggleShowHintsItem` now calls `executeAction`
- list it in the command palette's editor commands, next to `objectsSnapMode`
- document `appState.showHints` / `MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences.ToggleShowHints` in the CHANGELOG

`captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER`, matching `arrowBinding`/`midpointSnapping`. This is label-only in practice — `getObservedAppState` doesn't track `showHints`, so history never sees it either way.

## No keyboard shortcut

Deliberate. `arrowBinding` and `midpointSnapping` are also shortcut-less: these are set-once preferences, unlike zen mode / grid / view mode. The natural mnemonic `Alt+H` is already distribute-horizontally (`actionDistribute.tsx:88`). Consequently no `HelpDialog` row and no `shortcuts.ts` change — `getShortcutFromShortcutName` returns `""` for an unmapped name, which `actionToCommand` handles.

## Tests

New `tests/showHints.test.tsx` (6 tests): action registration under the `showHints` name, `checked()`, toggling, and the end-to-end effect on the rendered `.HintViewer`.

Verified the tests fail when the behaviour is reverted:

| reverted | result |
| --- | --- |
| the `if (!appState.showHints)` gate in `HintViewer` | 2 red |
| the `actions/index.ts` export | 4 red |

`yarn test:typecheck`, `yarn fix` (eslint `--max-warnings=0`) and the full vitest suite (140 files / 2287 tests) pass. No snapshot updates needed.

items.title: perf(editor): avoid rebuilding id sets on every drag
items.body:
Follow-up to #12180 (its "possible follow-up").

- `dragSelectedElements()` passed a fresh `Array.from(elementsToUpdate)` to every element's `updateBoundElements()` call. Each call therefore missed #12180's per-array ID-set cache and rebuilt a selection-sized set, so every drag step was O(n²) in the number of dragged elements, even without any arrows.
- The array is now built once per drag step and passed to every call. The unbinding checks reuse its cached set instead of building their own.
- `getSimultaneouslyUpdatedElementIds()` is exported for that. It documents the cache's contract: pass the same array instance for every element of one operation, and don't change its membership afterwards.
- Dragging N selected rectangles in the dev app (median frame time, same tab and window, Chrome):

  | N | before | after |
  | --: | --: | --: |
  | 1,000 | 45 ms | 18.5 ms |
  | 2,000 | 160 ms | 31 ms |
  | 4,000 | 643 ms | 54 ms |

- Tests cover grouped labels across z-order, frames with their children, bound arrows, bindings, unbinding and unchanged coordinates. One test fails if a call gets its own array again.

(opus-5-5, xhigh)

items.title: perf(editor): avoid rebuilding id sets on every resize
items.body:
## Problem

Resizing (or rotating) a large multi-selection gets slow. On every pointer move, `resizeMultipleElements()` calls `updateBoundElements()` once per selected element with the same `simultaneouslyUpdated` array, and `updateBoundElements()` rebuilds `new Set(simultaneouslyUpdated.map((el) => el.id))` on each call. That makes each pointer move O(n²), even when there are no arrows at all.

## Fix

`getSimultaneouslyUpdatedElementIds()` now caches the id set per `simultaneouslyUpdated` array in a `WeakMap`, so it is built once per pointer move instead of once per element. Call sites stay the same, and `rotateMultipleElements`, `alignElements` and `distributeElements` get the same speedup because they reuse one array the same way.

## Results

Time per pointer move when resizing a selection of N rectangles (no arrows) from the SE handle:

| N | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 500 | 10.9 ms | 2.2 ms |
| 1000 | 28.0 ms | 3.0 ms |
| 2000 | 135.1 ms | 5.7 ms |
| 4000 | 493.6 ms | 10.4 ms |

<sub>Measured with a throwaway vitest script that calls `resizeMultipleElements()` directly on a `Scene`. The script is not included in the PR.</sub>

The same scenario in the dev app, driven by Playwright. "Resize logic" is inclusive CPU-profiler time in `transformElements` per pointer move:

| N | resize logic before | resize logic after |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 | 88.0 ms | 3.5 ms |
| 4000 | 346.5 ms | 5.9 ms |

The full-frame numbers in the screenshots are high mainly because headless Chromium renders the canvas in software.

| Before (master) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|
| ![before 4000](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nicooga/excalidraw/aecbb95afaab6d8c2c4a7922d538352356e3eea0/before-4000.png) | ![after 4000](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nicooga/excalidraw/aecbb95afaab6d8c2c4a7922d538352356e3eea0/after-4000.png) |

## Testing

- `yarn test:typecheck` passes.
- Full `vitest` suite passes: 139 files, 2361 tests.
- eslint and prettier are clean.
- Behavior is unchanged: the before and after screenshots show the same resulting element sizes. Existing binding and resize tests cover the logic that skips simultaneously updated elements.

`dragElements()` passes `Array.from(elementsToUpdate)` inside its loop, so it creates a new array on every call and doesn't benefit from the cache yet. Hoisting that array out of the loop would fix drag the same way. It is left out of this PR to keep it focused on resize.

items.title: fix(editor): pan the canvas to follow the caret instead of shifting the UI
items.body:
Fixes #8936
Closes #8855
Closes #8119
Closes #10189
Closes #4688
Closes #9277
Closes #10585

- Typing with the caret past the viewport's edge made the browser scroll the editor root to reveal it, shifting the whole UI out of line with the canvas.
- The text editor's container is now the box a caret is revealed into: the canvas area, clipped, and kept off a docked sidebar. The browser scrolls that box instead, and the text editor turns the scroll into a canvas pan (plus 5px of room) and resets the box: nothing shifts, the caret comes into view, including one typed in behind a docked sidebar. Works full page and embedded; the host page never scrolls, iframes included.
- The text editor is no longer cut to the viewport (no max-width / max-height), so every text follows the same rule. A rotated text's editor now sits on the text (it rotates about the text's center).
- A free text that grows as you type now stops at the view's width (the canvas minus the sidebar, less 20px at each side, following the zoom) and wraps from there, so following the caret never pushes the text's start out of view (#8855). It stays anchored as it grew, and a text that's already wider keeps growing. Pasted text never wraps wider than that either.
- When a text starts wrapping, or a paste wraps, it's scrolled into view with the same 20px of room: a paste fully, and a typed text horizontally always but vertically only if it fits, so the view doesn't jump away from the caret.
- Internals: the scroll is a pure `scrollBoundsIntoView` (viewport.ts) applied with `viewport.translate`, so it respects scroll locks and stops following like a user pan. The sidebar is measured through the viewport UI markers (`AppViewport.getSidebarInsets`), and the width rule is an optional `maxWidth` on `refreshTextDimensions`.
- Limits: a caret above or left of the viewport isn't revealed (the editor's box can't scroll below 0). Verified in Chromium only.
- The editor root's CSS is unchanged: what a host does to its `overflow` no longer matters (tested with `visible`).
- Related: #8938 (fixes #8936 with `position: fixed`, which breaks non-full-page embeds).

items.body:
Surfaces library item names in the library sidebar and polishes library search.

## Changes

**Name tooltip on hover** (448ba16a2)
- Library items that have a name show it in a delayed tooltip above the item: after 500ms, or right away when moving over from another tooltip. It hides on pointer leave and on press.
- Driven by pointer events rather than mouse events, so a touch tap doesn't leave the tooltip behind. The mouse-driven hover state, which reveals the selection checkbox on tablets, is unchanged.
- `Tooltip` now exports `showTooltip()` / `hideTooltip()` (with a new `position: "top"` option) for elements that can't be wrapped in `<Tooltip>`; `<Tooltip>` itself uses them. Nothing is added per library item: no hooks, and the tooltip handlers are only bound for named items.
- A visible tooltip now hides when its target is removed from the DOM. No `pointerleave` fires in that case, so e.g. an item filtered out by the search, or the sidebar closing, used to leave a stale tooltip on screen. This uses a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` that only exists while a tooltip is visible. Measured in Chrome: ~0.5µs per DOM insertion/removal; hovering while a 500-item library renders in costs ≈0.75ms total; 0 when idle.

**Larger named items in search results** (2cd95915a)
- While searching, results render in 2 columns with larger previews and the item name below, ellipsified when it overflows. The whole card, name included, is clickable/draggable.
- In search results, the name tooltip only shows when the name is truncated.
- Placeholders match the card size, so nothing jumps while results render in batches.
- `scrollbar-gutter: stable` on the library list, so the content doesn't shift when results start/stop overflowing.

**Fix: Escape in library search closed the sidebar** (4218d19b6)
- With a search active in an undocked sidebar, Escape closed the sidebar instead of clearing the search. The input relied on the browser's native clearing of search inputs, and nothing stopped the event from reaching the Sidebar's document-level Escape listener.
- Escape now clears the search; a second Escape closes the sidebar.

## Testing

- `library.test.tsx`: Escape clears an active search without closing an undocked sidebar (failed before the fix), and Escape clears the item selection without closing it (already worked, now covered).
- Manually in Chrome with ~170 named items from real libraries: tooltip timing and placement, stale-tooltip cases (search filtering, sidebar close), click-to-insert from the card name, light and dark themes, phone width.
- Not tested in Firefox or Safari.

items.title: feat(editor): zen mode polish, hide toolbar hints preference & delayed canvas tooltips
items.body:
Closes #7421

A batch of canvas-UI polish, mostly around zen mode. Best reviewed per commit.

### Preference to hide toolbar hints

- New **Preferences → Show hints** checkbox, backed by `appState.showHints` (default `true`, browser-persisted, not exported). When off, `HintViewer` renders nothing.
- Exposed as `MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences.ToggleShowHints` for hosts composing their own preferences list.
- Snapshot updates are just the new `"showHints": true` key.

### Keep the main menu open when toggling view mode

Entering view mode ran `terminateActiveInteraction`, which reset `openMenu` and closed the main menu the user had just toggled view mode from (Preferences submenu). The main menu is available in view mode, so it's now only closed when interaction gets disabled (`interaction` prop).

### Zen mode

- **Hidden UI fades out in place** (opacity + visibility) instead of sliding off the viewport. It's non-interactive from the start of the fade (`pointer-events: none` on the subtree, since some children set their own) and unfocusable once hidden.
- **Visible canvas controls are chrome-less**: toolbar, main menu trigger, zoom, "Scroll back to content" and "Exit zen mode" drop their background/border/shadow. Hover/active states still apply. Popups and dialogs are unaffected.
- **Only the zoom level stays** out of the zoom controls, sliding into the zoom-out slot.
- **Fading the chrome without slowing hovers:** a permanent `background-color` transition would also delay hover backgrounds. So the chrome transitions only apply while `data-zen-mode-transition` is set on the container.
  - It's set in `getSnapshotBeforeUpdate`, i.e. before the DOM update. Layout reads during commit would otherwise resolve the new zen styles without the transition.
  - It's a data attribute so React doesn't drop it on re-render.
- A single `ZEN_MODE_TRANSITION_DURATION` (250ms) drives both the CSS (as `--zen-mode-transition-duration`) and the attribute's cleanup timer.
- Zoom and undo/redo button groups now paint one background on the group instead of one per button. The look is unchanged, and the zen fade animates the right layer.
- The reset-zoom button gets its own hover background. Unlike +/- it has no `.ToolIcon__icon`, and its old hover was only a side effect of the per-button background.

### Canvas button tooltips

- `Tooltip` gets a `delay` prop: it shows after 500ms, or immediately if a tooltip was visible within the last 300ms (moving across adjacent buttons). Passing over a button quickly no longer flashes a tooltip.
- Enabled for the zoom, undo/redo and help buttons.
- Zoom +/- use our `Tooltip` instead of a native `title`. Reset zoom drops its `title`, since it was showing both.
- `Tooltip` also takes a `className`, used to hide or shift the zoom wrappers in zen mode so the tooltip follows the element it belongs to.

### Notes

- Zoom +/- no longer carry the shortcut in their accessible description (it came from `title`). `aria-label` is unchanged.
- "Exit zen mode" keeps its own delayed fade-in timing.

---

Opus 5.5 (1M context), high

items.title: feat(editor): compact styles panel
items.body:
Makes the desktop styles panel more compact, and fixes two layout bugs that the content-sized panel exposed.

### Changes

- **Compact styles panel**
  - Buttons in the styles panel are always 32px. Before, they grew to 36px on screens wider than 1920px.
  - The gap between rows is 8px (was 12px).
  - Top-pick color swatches are packed tighter.
  - The panel now sizes to its content. `width: 12.5rem` became `max-width: 12.5rem`.
- **Large toolbar buttons on 1920px+ screens:** 40px → 38px, and the tool keybinding hint moved slightly.
- **Fix: Align buttons made the panel wider than its content.** The second row of align buttons was forced by a zero-height `flex-basis: 100%` spacer. That spacer only breaks the line during layout, so when the panel measured its natural width, both rows counted as one line (~240px). Any selection that showed Align widened the panel. Align is now two real flex rows.
- **Fix: opacity slider label went stale on resize.** The value label and the filled part of the track were computed in JS from the input's `offsetWidth`, and only when the value changed. Now that the panel width varies, the label ended up in the wrong place, sometimes overflowing the panel. Both are now positioned in CSS from a `--range-progress` variable. This also removes Chrome's default 2px inline margin on the input, which shifted the label off the thumb and pushed the track 2px past the panel's content edge.

### Notes

- The panel width now depends on its content. The sticky, frame and image tools (no color row) render a narrower panel (~176px vs ~195px). A `min-width` would pin it if we'd rather it didn't change width.
- When the panel is taller than the viewport, its scrollbar adds ~4px of width.

---
Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context), high

items.title: feat(editor): customizable font picker top picks
items.body:
Makes the font family top picks in the styles panel customizable, same as the color picker top picks (#11872):

- drag a font from the font picker list onto a top pick to replace it
- drag picks within the strip to reorder them
- right-click the strip, or use the new **Reset** link in the picker's tip, to restore the defaults

While dragging, the ghost is just the font's icon on a strip-button tile.

The tip in the color picker popups also gets the **Reset** link, shown when that picker's top picks are customized.

## Implementation

- The color picker's drag & drop is generalized into `components/TopPicksDnD/`: a value-agnostic `useTopPicksDnD<T>` hook, the reorder preview, the drop outline, the reset context menu, the tip with the reset link, and shared styles. Each picker has a thin adapter (`colorTopPicksDnD.ts`, `fontTopPicksDnD.ts`) that supplies value equality and the ghost visual. No behavior change for colors, except the new reset link.
  - Renamed: `startSwatchDrag` → `startSourceDrag`, and the `excalidraw-color-dnd-*` / `color-picker__context-menu` classes → `excalidraw-top-picks-dnd-*` / `top-picks-dnd__*`.
- New `appState.fontTopPicks: FontFamilyValues[] | null`. Like `colorTopPicks`, it is saved in the browser only, not in exports or on the server, and is kept when the canvas is cleared. On restore, unknown, internal and fallback families are dropped, duplicates are removed, and the list is capped at `FONT_TOP_PICKS_SLOTS` (3).
- Pinning doesn't apply the font. While a drag is in progress, fonts passed over in the list aren't live-previewed.

## Fixes along the way

- The font list's focus and pressed rings are now inset. The scrolling list clipped them at the sides and the next item covered their bottom edge, which became common now that you press and hold items to drag them.
- The ghost is now built on pointerdown. Previously it was built when the drag started, by which time the font list could have re-rendered on hover and detached the source row. A detached row measures as a zero rect, so a cancelled drag flew to the top-left of the viewport.

## Testing

- `FontPicker.test.tsx`: pinning from the list, refusing a font that's already pinned, reordering, and resetting from the tip.
- `fontTopPicks.test.ts`: restore validation.
- Snapshot updates are the new `fontTopPicks: null` key plus the shared class names on the color strip.

items.title: fix(editor): Binding follow-ups to #10753
items.body:
Follow-ups to #10753 from its review, now that it's merged.

- **Midpoint highlight color in dark mode.** The highlighted binding midpoint hardcoded `rgba(3, 93, 161)` for dark mode. That is the pre-filter color from when the interactive canvas was inverted by a CSS filter (`invert(93%) hue-rotate(180deg)` maps it exactly to `104, 182, 240`). The canvas now draws the final colors directly, so the dot rendered dark blue. It now uses `BINDING_HIGHLIGHT_RGB` like the rest of the binding highlight.
- **Midpoint visibility.** #10753 drew all four midpoints for any suggested binding, including simple arrows with the cursor deep inside the shape. This restores the previous rules:
  - simple arrows show no midpoints from inside the shape;
  - from outside, simple arrows show only the midpoint nearest the cursor, once it's within twice the binding distance;
  - elbow arrows show all four.

  The highlighted dot still comes from `suggestedBinding.midPoint`, so it sits where the arrow actually snaps.
- **Occlusion.** Only filled shapes hid the elements behind them from binding. Now:
  - images always count as opaque;
  - locked opaque elements hide what's behind them (they still can't be bound to);
  - frames are future-proofed: once they get a background, an opaque frame hides the non-children behind it. It doesn't stop the search, because its children sit just below it in z-order.

  Text stays see-through, since it has no fill.
- **`DEFAULT_ZOOM`.** A shared frozen `{ value: 1 }` zoom in `@excalidraw/common` replaces the scattered `{ value: 1 } as Zoom` fallback casts in elbow routing, `transform`, element rendering, binding repair on restore, and tests.

Tests: hit-test cases for image and locked occlusion. The frame case was checked by temporarily enabling frame backgrounds. The midpoint visibility was checked in the browser by recording the canvas draw calls for each case.

Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context), xhigh

items.title: feat(editor): wheel-button zoom and "zoom with scroll wheel" preference
items.body:
## Summary

Two wheel-navigation features, plus what fell out of building them.

- **Zoom by scrolling with the wheel (middle) button held down.** Same zoom as ctrl/cmd+wheel, anchored on the pointer. It wins over the modifiers and over the drag-pan the button itself starts, so a wheel-button pan can be zoomed one-handed without reaching for a key. Read off `event.buttons`, no extra state.
- **Input device preference** (`appState.inputDevice`: `"auto" | "mouse" | "trackpad"`, default `"auto"`, persisted to browser storage). A trackpad has a 2D pan gesture and a separate pinch (delivered as ctrl+wheel); a mouse has one notched axis and no pinch. With `"trackpad"` a plain wheel pans and ctrl/cmd+wheel zooms, as before; with `"mouse"` a plain wheel zooms and ctrl/cmd+wheel pans vertically instead, while shift+wheel keeps panning horizontally, a horizontal-only wheel (tilt wheel, sideways two-finger scroll) pans sideways, and the wheel-button zoom is unaffected. `"auto"` is reserved for detecting the device from the wheel events and resolves to `"trackpad"` through `resolveInputDevice()` until that exists. The preferences submenu gets a Trackpad / Mouse radio (also exported as `MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences.InputDevice`) that shows what `"auto"` resolves to.
- **Wheel handling extracted** from `App.tsx` into `App.wheel.ts` (`AppWheel`), in the same shape as the other `App.*` helpers.
- **Zoom-during-pan consistency.** Zooming mid-pan exposed three ways the point grabbed by the pan drifted from under the cursor, compounding per tick: the drag-pan wrote its scroll from `this.state` as a plain object and overwrote a zoom queued in the same React flush; a pointer move still waiting for its animation frame landed after the zoom; and the zoom updater read the anchor position when React evaluated it rather than when the wheel fired. All three are fixed, each pinned by a regression test. The same kind of stale read in `viewport.translate` made a pan queued behind a zoom tick count as a zoom and hard-clamp the rubberband overscroll to zero; `translate` is now a single updater that compares against the state it applies to. Zoom ticks that land on the zoom they started from (at the zoom limits) no longer flip the bitmap-cache flag and redraw the scene.
- **Zoom bitmap cache kept across pan frames.** `viewport.translate` cleared `shouldCacheIgnoreZoom` on every call, so every pan frame between two zoom ticks re-rasterized all elements at the in-progress zoom. With 1,200 rough shapes on screen, a 12-tick zoom with the pointer moving regenerated ~10k bitmaps with frames up to 283 ms; after the change it regenerates none and stays under 33 ms. The reset now happens only when a gesture interrupts an animated `setViewport`.
- **Wheel over a frame label is handled once.** The label's React `onWheel` duplicated the container's native listener, so wheel input over labels panned and zoomed twice per tick (pre-existing).

## Testing

- New `wheel.test.tsx` (11 tests) and two new cases in `scrollConstraints.test.tsx`; the full suite passes.
- Verified in Chrome with real pointer and wheel events: no drift of the grabbed point across ten interleaved move-and-zoom cycles, the mouse mode's modifier behavior, the bitmap-regeneration counts above, and single-step handling over frame labels.

fable 5.1

items.title: feat(editor): text tool edits what you click, shows what a click will do, drags out free text in shapes
items.body:
supersedes https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/11210

Makes the text tool act on what is under the cursor, and show it before the click.

## Interaction model

- **Clicking a text edits that text** — free text or a label, at the label's real position (arrow labels are hit where they are drawn, not at their stale stored coords).
- **Clicking elsewhere inside a labeled shape creates an independent text** at the click, no modifier needed (so it works on touch/pen too). Before, any click inside a labeled shape warped to the label and edited it.
- **Clicking an empty shape's center binds a label**, as before. **Dragging from the center creates a fixed-width free text instead**, sized by the drag, without provisionally enlarging small shapes. The decision waits for pointerup, so a jittery click still binds.
- **Hover shows what the click will do**: a dashed box around the text it would edit, the binding outline around the shape it would label, a point on the arrow anchor (free endpoint or midpoint label) it would attach text to. The cursor follows (text cursor over labels). Both stay current without the pointer moving: on Ctrl/Cmd press/release and when the viewport scrolls or zooms under a hovering mouse or pen (a lifted finger doesn't hover, so touch leaves nothing behind).
- **Ctrl/Cmd means "no binding"** for the whole text tool — endpoints and container labels alike. Production used Alt for the container opt-out; this aligns it with the rest of the editor (ported from #11210, thanks @lobre).
- Unbound text no longer inherits the `groupIds`/`angle` of the shape it happens to be created over.

## Implementation

- New `App.textTool.ts` (`AppTextTool`) owns the tool's pointer interaction. One resolver — endpoint → text → empty centered container → free — feeds the hover, the cursor and the pointerdown, so the affordance can never promise something the click won't deliver. The scene is hit-tested once per pointermove instead of twice.
- One AppState field `textToolHover` replaces `hoveredArrowTextAnchor` and the tool's previous borrowing of `elementsToHighlight`/`suggestedBinding` (which also made Ctrl/Cmd hide the container outline through the renderer's `isBindingEnabled` gate). Non-persisted; heads-up for hosts reading `hoveredArrowTextAnchor`.
- The pending center click lives in the helper (like `AppBucketFill`), `startTextEditing` takes an explicit `textElement` (so a host-selected text can't hijack a text-tool click elsewhere), and `getTextBindableContainerAtPosition` is purely positional; the double-click path keeps its selection preference inline and its own modifiers. The pending click is canceled when the tool is left (however it's left) and on pointercancel, so it can't be revived by re-picking the tool mid-press or resolved by unrelated movement; the outline it armed goes with it (also when a second finger turns the press into a pinch/pan).
- `hitElementItself` skips its cache for container-bound labels and tests labels at their derived position; `getTextElementWithAccuratePosition` is the one place that derives it.
- The dashed text box now redraws while drag-sizing under a locked text tool (`canvasNonce` folds in the new text's `versionNonce`, as it already did for framed elements).

## Changes beyond the text tool

- **Pointercancel tears the gesture down immediately** (`handleCanvasPointerCancel`), running the same cleanup a lost pointerup otherwise got at the next press. Left waiting, that replay tangled with the next press (a center click after a canceled one switched to selection and created nothing).
- **Only a genuine `pointerup` reverts an unlocked tool.** A replay by the missing-pointerup cleanup (a second finger landing, a pointercancel, the next press after a lost pointerup) only tears the gesture down, and leaves the tool to the press that follows. So after a lost pointerup, any unlocked tool now stays active instead of reverting to selection.

## Tests

- `textWysiwyg` and `arrowEndpointTextBinding`: hover states for every target, modifier press/release with a stationary pointer, center click vs. drag (mouse/pen/touch, small shapes, locked tool at 200% zoom, cancellation, container deleted mid-press, tool exit and re-pick mid-press, pointercancel, second finger), wheel scroll/zoom under a still pointer and after a lifted finger, cursor on modifier press/release, host-selected text/container, label hit-testing at 25/50/75% positions, dashed-box rendering while dragging.
- `collision`: cache regression for a label whose arrow moved.
- App-state snapshots updated for the field rename.

Related: #11210 (ported and credited), #5884 (related; not closed — it proposes dropping text-tool binding more broadly, this keeps click-to-bind).

(fable-5, fable-5-1, gpt-6-astra, opus-5-5 xhigh)

items.body: fix https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/9696 supersedes https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/10001 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cab08279-d57e-4c51-927c-e19d1cb8d8dd ## Summary A new `stickynote` element and tool (`N`): an always-filled, flat-rendered note whose label auto-fits. The font shrinks from the user's size down to a floor, and only then does the note grow. Notes are their own color domain, show their creation date in a footer, and are supported by the skeleton API. Builds on `element.created` from #12060. The pixel-snapping work that came out of this is #12063. ## How it works **Model.** A note is two elements: a `stickynote` container and one bound `text` label, on the existing bound-text machinery (wysiwyg editor, font and alignment actions, search, export). Two fields carry the user's intent. `baseHeight` on the note is the height the user gave it; `height = max(baseHeight, content)`, so a note never shrinks below its base and grows only when the label can't fit at the minimum font. `fontSizeMax` on the label is the font ceiling; the label's `fontSize` is the fitted, derived value. The note's width is the wrap width. **Layout.** One pure function, `getStickyNoteLayout(container, label, intents)`, is the single source of truth: it wraps the text at the note's width, fits the font under the ceiling (a grid of `STICKY_NOTE_FONT_STEP` anchored at the ceiling, warm-started binary search, floor at 16), grows the note past `baseHeight` only when the text still overflows at the minimum, and positions the label. It is applied through `updateStickyNoteLayout` (a live scene; runs the bound-arrow pass by default, callers forward `simultaneouslyUpdated` or opt out when they own one) and `relayoutStickyNotes` (an identity-preserving post-pass for immutable action results). Every recompute path goes through it: typing, paste, restore, resize, font actions, the skeleton API. **Resize intents.** `getStickyNoteResizeIntent` turns a gesture into absolute `baseHeight` / `fontSizeMax` intents from the gesture-start snapshot on every move: a width-only drag re-wraps, a height drag sets the base, a proportional resize (Shift on any handle, aspect-locked multi-select, a Stats group edit) scales the ceiling, anything else leaves the text size alone. North handles keep the bottom edge, Alt keeps the center. **Creation.** A click places a 250×250 note centered on the pointer. A drag is previewed at the true dragged size and snaps on release to a font-aware minimum (75, or one line at the current ceiling plus padding, plus the footer vertically), with the origin corner fixed; a Shift drag stays square. Editing starts right away. **Colors.** Notes are a separate domain: `currentItemStickynoteStrokeColor` (the note's ink, which is its text color) and `currentItemStickynoteBackgroundColor`, with their own customizable top-pick slots (`colorTopPicks.stickyNoteStroke` / `stickyNoteBackground`) and transparent excluded. `resolveColorTarget(appState, elements, property)` decides regular / sticky / mixed at execution time from the selection, the active tool and the label being edited, and drives the two pickers, both eyedroppers and paste styles; a mixed selection writes both domains. A note and its label share one ink: `syncStickyNoteInk` keeps the container's `strokeColor` and the label's equal after every write (the label wins on conflict, a transparent label takes the note's color). The stroke picker reads "Text color" for notes. **Creation-date footer.** Every note reserves a 32px band under the label body and paints `element.created` there as an absolute date, "7 Sep" while the year is the current one and "7 Sep 2025" otherwise, in the note's ink, on canvas and in SVG export. The form is chosen by width bucket rather than measured, so painting stays measurement-free (server-side SVG export has no text measurer). Fixed English, the viewer's local time zone (the exporter's for export). The band is reserved even when `created` is null; it just stays empty. **Rendering.** Flat: a solid fill with slightly jittered corners (seeded PRNG, now in `@excalidraw/common`), a drop shadow and an edge shadow, painted identically on canvas and SVG, with no roughjs involvement. The label renders as ordinary bound text. **Restore and API.** Restore clamps and seeds: `fontSizeMax` from `fontSize` when missing, non-transparent colors, the size floor, one ink per note; it refits geometry only under `refreshDimensions`. Skeleton: `{ type: "stickynote", x, y, label?: { text, fontSize? } }` creates a note with a fitted label (see the element-skeleton docs). **Toolbar.** The sticky tool sits on `N`. The image tool moved into "More tools" on desktop and tablet (mobile keeps its slot), and tool badges show the letter shortcuts since the numbered row is no longer contiguous; the number keys keep working. ## Things to be aware of - A note's `strokeColor` is its text color; no stroke is ever painted. Any code that writes a sticky label's `strokeColor` must write the container's too, or run `syncStickyNoteInk`, because the footer paints with it. - `fontSizeMax` is the user setting and `fontSize` is derived. Read and write font sizes through `getUserFontSize` / `getUserFontSizeUpdate`, which are container-aware; writing `fontSize` on a label directly is undone by the next layout. - `height >= baseHeight` always, and `baseHeight` only changes through height gestures, creation and Stats. Content growth never promotes into the base. - Two size floors: the data floor `STICKY_NOTE_MIN_SIZE` (75) that restore and the normalizers enforce, and the font-aware UI floor at creation and resize. - The footer reservation is unconditional and part of the layout (`STICKY_NOTE_BODY_INSET_Y`), so the editor, the fit and both renderers agree; footer metrics live in `STICKY_NOTE_FOOTER`. Dates are in the exporter's time zone in exports; no locale plumbing yet. - Arrows bound to a note follow its growth; exactly one bound-arrow pass runs per installing path. - Deferred on purpose: refitting notes when their font finishes loading (a note typed before the font loads keeps fallback-font geometry until the next edit); a sticky-specific palette beyond the top picks; a creator/ownership footer; localized dates. Pasting styles from a container onto free text drops the label's font styles, a pre-existing bug slated for the copy/paste-styles rewrite. ### vertical padding footer not included in the text padding offset by default (if there's enough space) so that it's visually vertically centered: ## Test plan - [x] `yarn test:typecheck`, ESLint, full vitest suite - [x] Element-level: layout and fit (termination, warm start, lowered ceilings, growth and shrink-back), resize intents across handles and modifiers, rotation, minimum sizes, date labels and width buckets, ink sync (34 tests) - [x] App-level: creation by click and drag, colors and eyedroppers in and out of edit mode, bound arrows through typing, resize, font changes and multi-select, paste styles, Stats, undo, SVG and canvas export with dates (24 tests), plus the color-target resolver, restore, skeleton, drag-create and created-timestamp suites - [x] Manual: create by click and by drag, type until the note grows, Shift-resize, pick colors while editing, both eyedroppers, export SVG and PNG with a dated note, dark mode (fable-5-1, gpt-6-astra)

items.title: feat(editor): snap element bitmaps, scroll and grid to whole device pixels
items.body:
## Summary

Three fixes for sub-pixel artifacts on the static canvas, one commit each.

**1. Element bitmaps blit on whole device pixels.** Elements are painted from cached bitmaps, blitted 1:1 with smoothing disabled for unrotated and right-angle elements. Nearest-neighbor at a fractional offset is a pixel-exact copy shifted to the nearest pixel — except at an exact half pixel, where a GPU-accelerated canvas decides the rounding per scanline by float precision: a few rows sample the neighboring row and glyph strokes come out doubled or broken, varying with scroll and position. A centered label lands on a half pixel routinely (odd free space ÷ 2), which is how it showed up on sticky notes. Measured in Chrome: a label blitted at `y = 639.5` had 3 of 82 scanlines taken from the adjacent row; rounded to 640 it was clean. The blit position is rounded through `context.getTransform()`, so it is exact at every zoom and canvas scale (rounding the pre-zoom value only lands on device pixels at 100%). Rotated elements are resampled regardless and are left alone; export draws directly and is unaffected. Cost: ~0.25 µs per element (`getTransform()` plus the math) next to ~2.3 µs for the `drawImage` it precedes.

**2. The canvases draw at a whole-device-pixel scroll.** Panning writes a fractional scroll (pointer delta ÷ zoom). With every bitmap landing on its nearest device pixel, a fractional scroll makes elements with different sub-pixel phases jump on different frames — a one-pixel wobble between neighbors, a label shifting against its box — and one scroll value in every pixel puts every integer-positioned element on the half-pixel boundary at once. The scroll is rounded at render time in the static, interactive and new-element renderers with the same formula, so overlays sit on the content; the real scroll in state is untouched, so hit-testing and DOM overlays are unaffected, and the difference stays under half a device pixel. Export is excluded.

**3. Grid lines on whole device pixels at every zoom.** The grid was nudged onto the pixel grid only at 100% and only when the scroll happened to be whole; at any other zoom its one-pixel lines rendered as two lighter pixels. Each line is now a whole number of device pixels wide and centered to cover them exactly, computed from the zoom and the canvas scale. Lines thinner than a device pixel (zoomed far out) keep their sub-pixel width on purpose: their lightness is what keeps the zoomed-out grid unobtrusive.

`imageSmoothingEnabled` stays disabled for these elements: it is what makes fractional offsets harmless in the first place; the snap closes the one hole nearest-neighbor leaves.

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn test:typecheck`, ESLint on every touched file, full vitest suite
- [x] `pixelSnap.test.tsx`: the static canvas's `drawImage` events (with their CTM) land on whole device pixels for text and a rectangle at zoom 1, 1.5, 0.73 and 2.2 under fractional scroll; a rotated element keeps its offset; the scroll helper rounds to device pixels and is identity when already whole; a rectangle at integer coordinates blits on whole pixels and a scroll a tenth of a pixel further lands on the same pixels; grid path starts sit on half device pixels at zoom 1, 1.5 and 2.2
- [x] Live in Chrome on the real (GPU-accelerated) static canvas: with the snap disabled, a label at a half-pixel offset shows the torn scanlines; with it, none. Scroll positions verified by intercepting `drawImage`: whole-pixel stepping at zoom 1, constant sub-pixel phase across four fractional scrolls at zoom 1.37
- [ ] Manual: type into a sticky note / centered label at a few scroll positions; pan slowly with the hand tool; grid at 150% and 75%

items.title: feat(editor): track element creation timestamps
items.body:
separated from https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/11847

Elements have a last-update timestamp but no independent creation time. This adds `created: number | null`, the client-clock creation time in epoch milliseconds of an element instance, and keeps `createdBy` / `updatedBy` and author-credit rules for a follow-up PR.

### Behavior

- New elements and copies with new IDs (duplicate, paste, library insertion) get a fresh creation timestamp. This describes the new instance, rather than the age of its source content.
- Edits, history capture, undo/redo and conversions that retain identity preserve the existing timestamp. Autoshape recognition preserves it while retaining the same element type/ID; replacing the element with a different type starts a new lifetime.
- Restoring a scene preserves known timestamps and maps missing values to `null`. An unknown creation time stays unknown: neither load time nor `updated` can reliably reconstruct it. Explicit `null` and `0` are preserved.

### Design decisions

Creation metadata is assigned during construction or duplication, before Store snapshot/delta capture. This keeps the live element and captured revisions consistent and avoids making capture time the birth time of an element created earlier in a gesture or stream. It requires no Store stamping, additional version bumps, transaction changes or author-credit machinery. The timestamp is descriptive metadata; collaboration conflict resolution continues to use the existing versioning rules.

`ElementUpdate` excludes `created`, making ordinary timestamp edits a type error. An explicit metadata repair must construct a replacement revision. Deltas still carry the field for replay, but creation-metadata-only differences do not count as visible changes or create separate undo steps.

Compatibility follows the conventions for other added element properties. Existing restore boundaries normalize incomplete runtime data, while import/export types, the `restoreElements` signature and the `updateScene` contract retain their existing shapes. A `created`-only optional input type or normalization shim would imply a special legacy-input guarantee for one field. General typing of raw import data belongs in a consistent, separate change. Hand-written complete element objects now need `created`, using `null` when unknown; existing scenes need no bulk backfill.

Freedraw, iframe and embeddable skeleton conversion now uses the standard constructors, so retained-ID inputs also receive defaults while preserving explicit timestamps. Regenerated IDs receive a fresh timestamp before construction. Label and endpoint fragment options exclude `created` because these fragments are constructed as new instances.

### Related boundary changes

- PNG scene embedding and JSON clipboard export restore their inputs, matching the existing canvas/SVG paths. All four paths are tested with legacy elements missing `created`.
- File loading restores elements once and uses that same result for scroll-to-content calculations. This also means imported-scene centering uses normalized geometry; bounds can differ when restore repairs or removes input elements.

### Validation

- Full suite: `yarn vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=1` — 125 files passed; 1,912 tests passed, 47 skipped, 1 todo.
- `yarn test:typecheck` passed.
- ESLint with `--max-warnings=0` passed on all changed TypeScript files.
- Coverage includes construction, duplication, skeleton conversion, legacy restore, library import, export, history, gesture creation and autoshape recognition; serialized snapshots and JSON schema documentation include the field.

(implemented by gpt-6-astra; unslopified by fable-5-1 and me)

items.title: fix(editor): dismiss dropdown menus on outside clicks
items.body:
Fixes a regression from #11974 where clicking the canvas or other UI no longer dismisses the main menu or More tools dropdown. The outside-click effect runs before Radix mounts the menu content, so it cannot resolve the owner document and never registers its listeners.

Track the mounted content node with a callback ref so outside-click listeners attach when the node becomes available. Also bind the Escape listener to the menu's owner document.

Validation:
- Added regression tests for both dropdowns covering outside pointer and touch events on the canvas and toolbar, including reopening. Both tests fail before the fix; all 3 dropdown tests pass afterward.
- Verified both menus at http://localhost:3002/ with UI clicks and canvas pointer events, including reopening.
- ESLint and git diff --check pass.

items.title: perf(editor): stop inverting the interactive canvas via CSS filter in dark mode
items.body:
## Problem

Users on Firefox/Zen reported the editor being laggy in dark mode only (light mode and Chrome fine). #10578 removed the CSS inversion filter from the static canvas, but the **interactive canvas** (selection outlines, transform handles, binding highlights, collaborator cursors, snap lines, scrollbars) was still composited through `filter: invert(93%) hue-rotate(180deg)` in dark mode. That canvas covers the whole viewport and repaints on nearly every pointer move, so browsers that composite in software pay for a full-viewport color-matrix pass per frame.

Reproduced in Firefox 154 with throwaway profiles (1920×1080 @ DPR 2, rAF frame timing during 150-step marquee/drag):

| profile | light | dark | dark, interactive filter removed |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (GPU WebRender) | 120 fps | 120 fps | 120 fps |
| `gfx.webrender.software=true` | 120 fps | 38 / 65 fps | 116–120 fps |
| `layers.acceleration.disabled=true` (HW accel off) | 120 fps | 42 / 64 fps | 120 fps |
| `gfx.canvas.accelerated=false` | 120 fps | 120 fps | 120 fps |

p95 frame time in the slow rows is a flat 33 ms (every other vsync dropped). Removing only the interactive-canvas filter restores full frame rate.

## Fix

Drop the CSS filter from `canvas.interactive` and map colors in JS via `applyDarkModeFilter`, the same approach as the static canvas:

- `interactiveScene.ts`: `getThemedColor` helper + tables for binding highlight / midpoint / search-match colors; every literal goes through it. The seven pre-compensated `THEME.DARK` ternaries are replaced by their actual post-filter colors.
- `renderSnaps.ts`: explicit dark / dark-zen snap colors instead of the pre-inverted red.
- `renderElement.ts` (`renderSelectionElement`): marquee fill themed.
- `theme.scss`: dark `--color-selection` now holds the actual rendered color (`#b4b0ff`, the post-filter value of the old `#3530c4`). The variable is only consumed by the canvas.
- `helpers.ts`: `getSelectionColor()` (reads `--color-selection` off any element inside the editor container, host overrides respected); `InteractiveCanvas.tsx` uses it.
- `lasso/index.ts`: lasso trail uses the same selection color (stroke + 5% fill) instead of a hardcoded light-theme purple. `common/colors.ts`: small `setColorAlpha` helper.
- `clients.ts`: drop the dark-mode speaking-color hack per the existing TODO.

All hardcoded dark constants were verified to equal `applyDarkModeFilter(<old value>)`.

## Visual changes

Rendering is pixel-identical (verified by screenshot diff in Chrome with a multi-selection in dark mode; only ~150 anti-aliased handle-edge pixels differ), except two intentional changes:

- collaborator cursors and remote selection outlines now render in the collaborators' actual colors (matching their avatars) instead of inverted ones
- the lasso trail now matches the marquee selection color in dark mode (it lives in the SVG overlay, which the filter never touched, so it was previously the light-mode purple on a dark canvas)

## Host note

If you override `--color-selection` for the dark theme, supply the actual color you want rendered — it is no longer inverted.

Closes #2346, closes #6876, closes #7332

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn test:typecheck`
- [x] `yarn test:update` (123 files / 1872 tests, no snapshot changes)
- [x] Firefox software-WebRender profile: dark mode back to 120 fps with the filter removed
- [x] Chrome: before/after screenshot diff of selection UI in dark mode; lasso stroke/fill attributes `#b4b0ff` / `#b4b0ff0d` in dark mode

items.title: fix(editor): detect line height from the migrated font props on restore
items.body:
### What breaks

`restoreElement`'s text branch migrates the legacy `font` prop into local `fontSize` and `fontFamily` variables, but the line-height detection right below it kept reading `element.fontSize` and `element.fontFamily`. A diagram old enough to carry `font` has neither of those props, so `detectLineHeight` computed `height / lineCount / undefined` and the element came back with `lineHeight: NaN`.

```ts
const element = {
  type: "text",
  font: "20px Virgil", // legacy prop, no fontSize/fontFamily/lineHeight
  text: "hi",
  height: 50,
  // ...
};

restoreElements([element], null)[0].lineHeight; // NaN, expected 2.5
```

`NaN` then flows into `getLineHeightInPx` and every height computation derived from it, and it is written back out on the next save.

The same code path produced `NaN` whenever `height` was not a number, and `Infinity` when `fontSize` was `0`.

### Why here

The detection is meant to recover the original line height of old diagrams, so it has to read the values that migration produced rather than the raw element. Moving it into `restoreLineHeight` keeps the call site short and puts the fallback next to the detection: if the detected value is not a finite positive number, use the font family's fixed line height, which is what the `element.height` falsy branch already did.

The detection stays behind `element.lineHeight ||`, so it is still skipped for elements that already carry a line height; evaluating it eagerly breaks elements whose `text` is `null`.

### Before

```
 × restoreElements > should detect the line height of a text element that only has the legacy font prop
   → expected NaN to be 2.5 // Object.is equality
 × restoreElements > should fall back to the font line height when it can't be detected
   → expected false to be true // Object.is equality

      Tests  2 failed | 51 passed (53)
```

### After

```
yarn vitest run packages/excalidraw/tests/data/restore.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  53 passed (53)

yarn vitest run packages/excalidraw/tests/data packages/element/tests
 Test Files  26 passed (26)
      Tests  603 passed | 35 skipped | 1 todo (639)
```

`tsc --noEmit -p packages/excalidraw/tsconfig.json`, `eslint` and `prettier --check` on both files are clean.

### Not changed

While checking this path with deliberately broken elements I also saw `restoreElements` pass through a non-finite `fontSize`, `x` and `opacity` unchanged, and drop the element entirely when the legacy `font` prop is not a string (`font.split` throws). Those are separate from line-height detection, so they are left alone here.

items.title: feat(packages/excalidraw): support rendering into another document
items.body:
## Summary

- add an optional, stable `ownerDocument` prop to the Excalidraw component
- route editor-owned listeners, DOM creation, fonts, text editing, and window APIs through that document and its `defaultView`
- make shared DOM guards work with elements from another browsing context
- preserve the existing global-document behavior when the prop is omitted

## Motivation

Hosts can render a fresh Excalidraw root into another document while sharing one evaluated React and Excalidraw runtime. Today, multi-window Electron apps and iframe-style integrations otherwise need to evaluate a separate package runtime in every window because pointer and keyboard listeners, DOM constructors, fonts, and WYSIWYG editing bind to the document where the package was evaluated.

Using an instance-scoped document avoids a mutable global context and supports multiple editors in different documents at the same time. In Obsidian this removes the need for a roughly 90 MB-class Excalidraw runtime per popout window and substantially simplifies window lifecycle ownership.

The intended model remains: create a new React root for the destination document; do not move an existing React tree across windows.

## Compatibility and risk

`ownerDocument` is optional and defaults to the current global `document`, so existing integrations retain their current path. The value is documented as stable for the mounted editor lifetime.

The changes are limited to APIs whose ownership must match the rendered editor: event registration and cleanup, DOM creation and selection, fonts, realm-specific constructors, observers, timers, and animation frames.

## Validation

- added a cross-document iframe test covering editor initialization plus pointer, keyboard, paste, window-message, and font listener ownership
- added cross-realm DOM utility coverage
- full test suite: 123 files, 1862 passed, 47 skipped, 1 todo
- typecheck passed
- targeted ESLint passed
- `build:excalidraw` passed
- manually validated a shared runtime with fresh editor roots in the main document and an Electron popout, including pointer drawing, text editing and fonts, undo, popovers, and Escape handling

items.title: fix(editor): handle the save-as shortcut while editing text
items.body:
Fixes #11914

## Summary

Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+S did nothing while a text element was being edited — the editor stayed open and no save happened. Plain Cmd/Ctrl+S worked in the same state.

The wysiwyg keydown handler only branches on `actionSaveToActiveFile`, whose `keyTest` requires `!event.shiftKey`. `actionSaveFileToDisk` — which owns the shift variant — was never handled there, and wasn't even imported, so the event matched no branch and was swallowed.

This adds the sibling branch, mirroring exactly what the plain shortcut already does: commit the text, then run the action.

Complements #9281, which fixed the plain shortcut in this same handler.

## Tests

Two added to `packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx`:

- `commits the editor on Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+S` — pins the fix. Reverting it fails with `expected { id: 'id1', type: 'text', … } to be null`, i.e. the editor stayed open.
- `still commits the editor on plain Cmd/Ctrl+S` — control. It passes with the fix reverted, which isolates the bug to the shift variant.

```
yarn vitest run packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx
```

80/80 pass. `yarn test:typecheck` clean.

fix(editor): respect boxSelectionMode ('contain' vs 'overlap') in lasso tool
items.body:
Closes #11809

> ⚠️ **Note:** This PR has one pre-existing failing test in `selection.test.tsx` unrelated to this fix. It is already resolved in **#11861** — please merge **#11861 first**.

---

## Problem

The freeform lasso tool always selected elements in **"overlap"** mode — selecting anything its path touched — completely ignoring the user's **"Select on wrap vs overlap"** preference in settings.

This toggle worked correctly for the **rectangle** selection tool but had **zero effect** on the lasso tool.

---

## Root Cause

Two issues in `packages/excalidraw/lasso/utils.ts`:

1. `getLassoSelectedElementIds()` had no `mode` parameter — it couldn't know the user's preference.
2. `enclosureTest()` always used `.some()` logic — classifying an element as "enclosed" if even **one point** fell inside the lasso. This is wrong for `"contain"` mode where **all points** must be fully inside.

---

## Fix

### `lasso/utils.ts` — Fixed `enclosureTest` to use `.every()` for contain mode

```ts
if (mode === "contain") {
  // ALL points must be inside the lasso polygon
  return segments.every((segment) =>
    segment.every((point) => polygonIncludesPointNonZero(point, lassoPolygon))
  );
}
// overlap: original behavior preserved
return segments.some((segment) =>
  segment.some((point) => polygonIncludesPointNonZero(point, lassoPolygon))
);
```

### `lasso/index.ts` — Pass user preference through selection flow

```ts
const { selectedElementIds } = getLassoSelectedElementIds({
  ...
  mode: this.app.state.boxSelectionMode,
});
```

### `lasso.test.tsx` — Fixed tests + added new coverage

- Fixed `beforeEach` to explicitly initialize `boxSelectionMode: "overlap"` so all 6 original tests run with their intended behavior.
- Added a new `Special cases` test verifying both `contain` and `overlap` modes work correctly.

---

## Demo


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86e03e9a-f034-433d-9d17-134f4db035c3


---

## Verification

```bash
yarn test packages/excalidraw/tests/lasso.test.tsx
```

```
✓ lasso.test.tsx   7/7 tests passed
✓ yarn test:typecheck — 0 errors
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/excalidraw/lasso/utils.ts` | Fixed `enclosureTest` with `.every()` for contain mode; added `mode` param |
| `packages/excalidraw/lasso/index.ts` | Pass `mode: this.app.state.boxSelectionMode` |
| `packages/excalidraw/tests/lasso.test.tsx` | Fixed `beforeEach`; added `boxSelectionMode` test |

items.title: feat(packages/excalidraw): ViewportStatusFrame & factor out user-follow state

labels.name: s-package
labels.description: scope: package (related to packages/* API, not necessarily user facing)

items.body:
# feat: `ViewportStatusFrame`, hoist follow state, `currentUserControls`

## Summary

- Replaces the internal `FollowMode` component and PR #10926's `canvasNotification` prop with a single **`ViewportStatusFrame`** component/prop — one viewport-edge border + bottom-center badge, host-composed.
- **Hoists `userToFollow`/`followedBy` out of `appState`** to host-controlled state. The editor no longer decides who you're following — it only emits follow/unfollow *intents* (via `onUserFollow`, prop or imperative API) and renders whatever `userToFollow` the host passes back in.
- Redesigns `UserList`'s "who's here" UI: one merged dropdown (own avatar as trigger) instead of a separate `currentUserMenu` pill + `+N` overflow popover.
- Adds `currentUserControls`: host-rendered content in that dropdown (and now the mobile menu too), accepting either a node or `(isMobile: boolean) => ReactNode`.
- Ports `excalidraw-app`'s `Collab` to the new controlled model.

## Breaking changes

- `AppState.userToFollow` / `AppState.followedBy` removed. Use the new `userToFollow` prop (controlled) instead.
- `FollowMode` component removed; its badge/border is now whatever `viewportStatusFrame` the host composes (see `excalidraw-app/App.tsx` for the reference "Following X" badge).
- `onUserFollow` (prop and imperative API) now fires **only on user-initiated gestures** (avatar click, badge close, canvas pan/zoom/pointerdown breaking follow) — never on host-driven `userToFollow` prop changes. Consumers that relied on it firing for every state transition need to update.
- `canvasNotification` renamed to `viewportStatusFrame`; shape changed — `label`/`icon`/`background`/`color`/`onClose` now nest under `label`, and `border` is a required `false | string` (no default-color boolean variant).
- `currentUserMenu` renamed to `currentUserControls`.

## Details

- **`ViewportStatusFrame`** (`packages/excalidraw/components/ViewportStatusFrame/`): border overlay + badge, `role="status"`, real close `<button>`.
- **Follow-intent plumbing**: `App.emitUserFollowIntent`/`App.requestUnfollow` replace direct `appState.userToFollow` writes across `actionNavigate.tsx` (avatar click), the six zoom/fit actions in `actionCanvas.tsx`, and pan/pointerdown in `App.tsx`/`App.viewport.ts`. Laser pointer pointerdown is excluded — it's a presentation aid, not an edit, and shouldn't break follow.
- **`excalidraw-app/collab/Collab.tsx`**: new `userToFollowAtom` + `setUserToFollow` funnel (handles leaving the old follow room before joining the new one); `followedBy` moved to a Collab class field. Own collaborator entries are now seeded with the local username (`setCollaborators`/`updateCollaborator`/`setUsername`) — collaborators never receive their own broadcasts, so without this the current user's entry had no username and got filtered out of `UserList`.
- **`UserList` redesign**: current user's avatar is always rendered as a pill (avatar + chevron), reserved its own slot so it's never hidden by or orphaned from overflow. Its dropdown always lists every collaborator (self included — "if you're alone, show just yourself") plus `currentUserControls` below a divider. Self's row shows `(You)` and is inert (no hover/click). Mobile menu gets the same `currentUserControls` content, inline. Fixed a layout bug where the trigger could wrap onto its own line when avatars didn't fit an integer number of slots.
- **Debug aid**: `excalidraw-app/debugCollaborators.ts` — `useSimulatedCollaborators` hook, dev-only, populates N static fake collaborators via `?collaborators=<N>` (one marked as the current user) for exercising this UI without a real collab room.

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn test:typecheck`, `yarn test:code` (lint), full suite (`yarn test:update`) all green
- [x] Manual: follow/unfollow via avatar click, badge close, canvas pan/zoom/pointerdown; followed user leaving the room auto-unfollows
- [x] Manual: `UserList` dropdown solo / with overflow / at various widths; `currentUserControls` on desktop and mobile
- [x] Manual: `?collaborators=N` debug flag

- Manually verified using the exact scene JSON from the issue: imported via File → Open, selected the arrow, right-clicked → "Edit arrow". This did not crash.
- Manually verified the original repro end-to-end on macOS: created an arrow via Mermaid → Excalidraw, duplicated it via Option (⌥)+drag, then right-clicked the duplicate → "Edit arrow". This did not crash.
