items.title: feat(editor): bind text to hovered arrow endpoint
items.body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d8b9d42-2d9e-45df-93a2-199bbd7b4806

(implemented with Opus 5)

↓↓↓ AI notes ↓↓↓

----

# Bind text to an arrow endpoint

Lets you label the tip of an arrow: with the text tool active, hovering a free arrow endpoint highlights it, and clicking creates a text element bound to that endpoint.

The arrow is treated as fixed. Rather than routing the arrow to the text, we pick the side of the text the arrow should attach to — the one it already points at — and place the text so that side's midpoint lands on the existing endpoint. The arrow doesn't move, at creation or while typing.

| arrow reaches the tip heading | text sits | bound side | textAlign / verticalAlign |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| up | above | bottom | center / bottom |
| down | below | top | center / top |
| right | to the right | left | left / middle |
| left | to the left | right | right / middle |

Also highlights the **label midpoint** when hovering the arrow itself, so both things the text tool can do to an arrow are visible.

## Details

- **Alignment does the anchoring.** `getAdjustedDimensions` already pinned the text horizontally by `textAlign` while typing; it hardcoded `s: true` vertically. Generalising that to `verticalAlign` means a bottom-bound text grows upward and a middle-bound one grows symmetrically, so the bound side midpoint stays put as you type. `verticalAlign` is inert on unbound text, so it's free to carry the vertical anchor exactly as `textAlign` carries the horizontal one.
- **The anchor is placed along the arrow's line, not the side's normal.** `updateBoundPoint` resolves an orbit binding by intersecting the arrow's own line with the target outline grown by `gap`. Offsetting along the normal instead leaves the tip `gap · tan θ` off to one side — invisible on orthogonal arrows, ~5px on diagonal ones, and only once the first keystroke triggers `updateBoundElements`. Walking back along the arrow keeps the anchor both `gap` clear of the tip and collinear with it, so the intersection returns to the tip exactly.
- **Gap comes from the text, not the arrow.** `getBindingGap` takes its stroke component from the bind target, so anchoring with the arrow's stroke width shifted the tip by half the difference whenever the two differed — which is common at default settings.
- **Drag to set max width.** Same as free text. Placement stays whatever the binding decided; only the width follows the pointer, growing away from the arrow. Dragging back toward the arrow makes no progress rather than flipping the box over it.
- **Ctrl/cmd** suppresses the endpoint affordance and the binding, like every other arrow binding. A label is a container binding, so it is unaffected.
- **Occlusion.** The endpoint scan only knows about arrows, so it would reach through anything drawn on top; an element stacked above the arrow that the pointer actually hits now owns the click.

## Fixes to existing behaviour

**Creating a text opened two history entries.** The empty element, then its content — so the first undo restored a live, zero-content element (invisible, and for a bound text still holding the binding). Creating a text reverts the tool to `selection` during pointerdown, so the pointerup that follows looked like an ordinary canvas click and captured the still-empty element. Pointerup has two such capture sites and they don't both fire in every environment — jsdom hits one, the browser the other — so both are now gated on a text being in flight. This affects **all** text creation, not just bound text.

**The autoResize handle ignored alignment.** It recomputed width/height but never touched `x`/`y`, so the box always grew from its top-left and a right-aligned or centred text slid sideways. It now anchors by alignment, and calls `updateBoundElements` — the anchor can only pin one point, so any other arrow bound to the same text still has to be re-routed.

## Refactors

Extracted rather than duplicated, each because a second or third caller appeared:

- `getTextAnchorRatios` — the alignment→anchor-ratio table, previously inside `getTextElementPositionOffsets` and re-encoded as the `n/s/e/w` flags in `getAdjustedDimensions`; now also used by the drag and the autoResize handle.
- `dragNewTextElement` — both text drag paths are the same operation (pin a point, grow away from it) differing only in where the ratio comes from: drag direction for free text, alignment for bound. The directional clamp falls out of the ratio being fixed rather than needing a special case.
- `LinearElementEditor.getBoundTextElementCenter` — pulled out of `getBoundTextElementPosition`; `getContainerCenter`'s arrow branch now delegates to it. Its `getEditorMidPoints` lookup was a no-op (it returns either `null` or exactly the fallback value), so this also drops an unnecessary `appState` dependency from a geometry helper. Makes "the highlight is where the click lands" structural rather than coincidental.
- `applyBinding` — the write-binding-plus-record-on-target bookkeeping, previously duplicated.
- `highlightPoint` absorbed the `save/translate/restore` wrapper that four call sites repeated.

## Notes

- `appState.hoveredArrowTextAnchor` is new (`{ elementId, anchor: "start" | "end" | "label" }`). It's render-only — the click path recomputes from scratch — and is transient, so it doesn't re-render the UI. Kept separate from `suggestedBinding` deliberately: that one is gated on `isBindingEnabled` and means "the element that will be bound *to*", whereas an endpoint anchor is where a click will *act*, with no target yet.
- The label anchor is offered only when the click would actually produce a label, i.e. when it also snaps to the arrow's centre — `getTextBindableContainerAtPosition` resolves an arrow anywhere in its bounding box, which would over-promise.
- Snapshot churn is the one new appState key.

## `props.activeTool`

Controlled prop that forces the active tool: `activeTool={{ type: "laser" }}` (or `{ type: "custom", customType: ... }`).

- User/API tool switching is refused at the `setActiveTool` funnel; funnel-bypassing writers (restore, finalize) are corrected by an edge-triggered sync in `componentDidUpdate`.

## `interaction.enabled.tools`

New exception under `interaction={{ enabled: ... }}`: listed tools (`laser`, `custom`) remain user-activatable while the editor is otherwise non-interactive. Enables the presentation use case — presenter draws with the laser on an otherwise inert canvas, and `savePointer` stays live so collab viewers see the trail.

- `isToolSupported()` is now the single predicate for "can this tool be activated" — folds the `UIOptions.tools` axis and the `interaction` axis.

- Invariant: while non-interactive, the active tool auto-resets to `selection` when it loses its exception.

items.body:
fix https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/11591
close https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/11606

implemented by fable-5 (xhigh)

Notes from fable:

> ## Problem
> 
> #11492 switched labeled arrows on export from a temp-canvas blit to direct vector drawing (fixing high-scale blur), but kept the "punch the label hole afterwards" model. On a shared export canvas that's destructive: the hole is `fillRect`-ed with the view background color (or `clearRect`-ed when transparent), painting over / erasing whatever is rendered **beneath** the arrow. The editor was unaffected, so exports stopped matching the canvas.
> 
> ## Fix
> 
> Cut the hole out of the arrow's own strokes instead of out of the scene: establish an even-odd clip (generous outer rect minus the label rect, axis-aligned in scene space) **before** drawing the arrow. The arrow simply never paints under the label; elements beneath show through, and #11492's direct-vector sharpness is fully preserved (no temp canvas, no resampling).
> 
> ## Follow-up: same trick in the editor path
> 
> With the hole applied at blit time, the editor's `boundTextCanvas` mechanism (a **square `maxDim²` canvas** per labeled arrow that baked rotation + hole, bypassing all size caps — up to GB-class requests for long thin arrows) becomes unnecessary and is removed:
> 
> - labeled arrows blit through the ordinary rotated path under one extra clip;
> - `angle` and `boundTextElementVersion` dropped from the canvas-cache key → rotating a labeled arrow no longer re-rasterizes it per pointermove (2 canvas allocs → 0), label keystrokes re-raster only the text itself (3 → 1);
> - the dormant default-size canvas + 2D context previously allocated for **every** cached element of every type is gone.
> 
> ## Testing
> 
> - New regression test: exporting a labeled arrow over a filled rectangle must never `fillRect`/`clearRect` a hole-sized region and must clip with `evenodd` (fails on `master`).
> - Manually verified on canvas exports: light / dark / transparent background, rotated arrows, multi-line labels, 4× export scale (pixel-sharp); editor verified at zoom 1–2 incl. rotation and live label editing.

 Extremely large arrows (issue #11497, stop-gaps in
newElement.ts / elbowArrow.ts normalizeArrowElementUpdate / restore.ts
MAX_LINEAR_PX) are caused by **binding to a zero/near-zero-size bindable
element**:

- `calculateFixedPointForNonElbowArrowBinding` and
  `calculateFixedPointForElbowArrowBinding` (binding.ts) compute
  `ratio = (point - element.x) / Math.max(element.width, PRECISION)` with
  PRECISION = 1e-4, and the arrow endpoint sits a **fixed ~5px binding gap**
  (`getBindingGap`, BASE_BINDING_GAP=5) outside the outline → for a 0-size
  element ratio ≈ -5/1e-4 = **-50,000**.
- `normalizeFixedPoint`/`isFixedPoint` only check finiteness, never range, so
  the poison ratio persists in the document.
- When the bound element is later resized to normal size,
  `getGlobalFixedPointForBindableElement` computes
  `x + width * ratio` → endpoint millions of px away. Affects both simple and
  elbow arrows (both use fixedPoint).

items.body:
fix https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/3686
close https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/7085 (superseded)

# feat: `interaction` & `ui` props

Adds two host-controlled props for disabling UI, or [partially] disabling user interaction.

```tsx
<Excalidraw
  interaction={{ enabled: { navigation: true, interactiveContent: true } }}
  ui={false}
/>
```

## `interaction`

`boolean | { enabled?: { navigation?; links?; embeds?; interactiveContent?; browserZoom? } }`

- `interaction={false}` makes the editor fully inert to user input — no panning/zooming (pointer, wheel, keyboard, pinch), selecting, editing, keyboard shortcuts, clipboard, context menu, or drag&drop. Implies view mode (`appState.viewModeEnabled` reports `true` and can't be unset while non-interactive). The scene still renders and stays fully controllable through the imperative API (`updateScene`, `setViewport`, …), so hosts can drive live previews, thumbnails, presentations, and annotation overlays.
- Since wheel/touch input is no longer captured, the page scrolls naturally over the editor; the browser's own zoom is still prevented over it by default.
- Keys under `enabled` are opt-in exceptions (additive):
  - `navigation` — view-mode-style pan & zoom (drag, wheel, pinch, and the canvas zoom / zoom-to-fit shortcuts). Respects `appState.scrollConstraints`, so it composes with viewport locking (#11554) for constrained viewers.
  - `links` — link icons render and linked elements open their link on click, view-mode style. When disabled, link icons aren't rendered at all.
  - `embeds` — embeddable & iframe elements stay activatable/usable, view-mode style.
  - `interactiveContent` — shorthand for `links` + `embeds` (and future interactive content kinds).
  - `browserZoom` — opts back into the browser's own zoom over the editor (moot with `navigation`, which consumes zoom input).

Internally, `App` exposes capability getters (`interactionEnabled`, `navigationEnabled`, `linksEnabled`, `embedsEnabled`) that all input entry points consult — listeners are simply not attached where possible, with entry guards and an `ActionManager` gate (keyboard + non-`api` `executeAction`) backing them up. Actions can declare `navigation: true` (analogous to `viewMode`) to stay available in navigation mode.

## `ui`

`boolean` — when `false`, Excalidraw's default UI is not rendered (toolbar, default menu/footer controls, sidebars, canvas popups, context menu). Canvas content (elements, text editing surface, frame names, embeds) still renders, and the editor stays interactive unless `interaction` says otherwise. Host children still mount (they may be functional, e.g. a collab component), and host-supplied UI built from exported components (`<MainMenu>`, `<Footer>`, …) continues to render.

## Related behavior changes

- Zoom-to-fit shortcuts (`shift+1/2/3`) are no longer disabled under a viewport lock — with no selection they now fit the **locked box** (i.e. return to the lock's resting viewport), re-clamped against the lock; `zoomToFitSelection(InViewport)` also gained `viewMode: true`, so `shift+2/3` work in view mode (falling back to fit-all).

## Root cause

\`getOffsets\` in \`packages/element/src/flowchart.ts\` used parity-based offsets derived from \`element.width\` / \`element.height\`. It did not look at the actual positions or sizes of the already-existing sibling nodes, so the math only happened to work when every sibling was created in the original session with the default dimensions.

## Fix

When existing siblings are present and the "free space" early-return doesn't apply, compute the bounding box of the sibling row/column and place the new node past it with a constant \`HORIZONTAL_OFFSET\` / \`VERTICAL_OFFSET\` gap, aligning the new node with the existing row.

The side (right vs left for up/down direction, below vs above for left/right direction) is chosen to keep the chart balanced around the parent's center.

## Test

Added a regression test in \`packages/element/tests/flowchart.test.tsx\` that creates four children of a 400×300 node one at a time and asserts:

- all four siblings share the same y coordinate (no misalignment)
- no two siblings overlap horizontally

All existing flowchart tests still pass, as does the rest of the \`packages/element\` suite (459 tests).

## Problem
When converting between generic shapes, the roundness type was only recalculated when the target type was a diamond. items.title: fix(editor): narrow `NonDeleted` type to `isDeleted: false`
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #6746

The `NonDeleted<T>` generic used `isDeleted: boolean`, which made it structurally identical to the base `ExcalidrawElement` type — it provided no type safety. This PR changes it to `isDeleted: false` so TypeScript actually enforces the non-deleted contract at compile time:

```ts
export type NonDeleted<TElement extends ExcalidrawElement> = TElement & {
  isDeleted: false;
};
```

Supersedes the abandoned #11088.

## What changed

The core change is 1 line in `packages/element/src/types.ts`. Since the type was previously a no-op, narrowing it surfaced ~375 typecheck errors; each was resolved with the smallest fix that keeps the types honest (no behavior changes — see the one exception below):

1. **Generic type guards** (`typeChecks.ts`) — guards like `isTextElement` now have the form `<T extends ExcalidrawElement>(element: T | null): element is T & ExcalidrawTextElement`, so they preserve `NonDeleted` (and other intersections such as `Ordered`) through `.filter()` chains and `if` narrowing instead of widening back to the base type. No runtime logic changed.

   > Note: overloads (as #11088 described) don't work here — when an overloaded guard is passed as a callback, TS resolves it against the last signature, which silently breaks `.filter()` narrowing. The generic intersection form is sound for both plain and `NonDeleted` inputs.

2. **Honest producers** — APIs that only ever produce non-deleted elements now say so: element creation (`newElement.ts`), `getSelectedElements`, `duplicateElements`, `LinearElementEditor.getElement`, and the test helper `API.createElement`.

3. **Parameter widening** — functions that accept `NonDeleted<T>` but never need the guarantee were widened to `ExcalidrawElement`: rendering (`renderElement`, `renderElementToSvg`, …), coordinate/bounds math, frame membership, z-index, group selection, resize helpers. Pure filters (`getElementsWithinSelection`, `elementsOverlappingBBox`, `getRootElements`, `syncInvalidIndices`, …) are now generic so they preserve the input element type.

4. **Targeted casts** at boundaries where elements are known to be non-deleted at runtime but the type system can't infer it (e.g. lookups from `getNonDeletedElementsMap()`, freshly duplicated selections), each with a short comment.

### One deliberate behavior alignment

`packages/utils/src/export.ts` (public `exportToCanvas`/`exportToSvg`/`exportToBlob`) now drops deleted elements after `restoreElements(..., { deleteInvisibleElements: true })`, matching the editor's own export path (`prepareElementsForExport`). Previously, elements marked deleted were skipped by the SVG renderer but still rendered on canvas exports and included in export-bounds computation. Happy to split this into a separate PR if preferred — without it, the call sites would need a cast that lies about the restored elements.

## Testing

- [x] `yarn test:typecheck` — clean
- [x] `yarn test:update` — 102 test files, 1385 tests passing, **zero snapshot diffs** (confirms the change is type-only)
- [x] `yarn test:code` — clean
- [x] `yarn build:packages` — all packages build
- [x] Added type-level tests in `packages/element/tests/typeChecks.test.ts` (`@ts-expect-error` assertions that deleted/unnarrowed elements are no longer assignable to `NonDeleted`, plus `.filter()` narrowing checks)

items.title: fix(editor): ensure canvas is cleared when background color is invalid to prevent ghosting
items.body:
Resolves #10931

## User Impact
An invalid viewBackgroundColor value can cause the canvas to stop clearing correctly during panning, leaving visual trails from previous frames and making the canvas difficult to use.
This PR makes canvas rendering more resilient to invalid background color values, including cases where persisted state becomes corrupted.

## Root Cause
In bootstrapCanvas, an invalid value such as "0000":
1. Does not trigger the transparency path because its length is not zero.
2. Is not a valid CSS color value.
3. Causes the background fill operation to fail, leaving previously rendered content visible.
4. Results in the "ghosting" effect reported in the issue.

## Fix
* Added validation for viewBackgroundColor before it is used by the renderer.
* Invalid color values are treated as transparent during the clearing phase.
* When validation fails, the canvas is cleared using context.clearRect() to prevent rendering artifacts.
* Improved type narrowing in staticScene.ts for safer access to background state properties.

## Verification
### Manual Testing
Injected invalid values such as "0000" and "abc" into LocalStorage and confirmed that:
* Invalid values are detected correctly.
* The renderer falls back to clearRect().
* No ghosting artifacts occur during panning

### Regression Testing
Verified that:
* Valid hex colors render normally.
* Transparent backgrounds continue to work as expected.
* Light and dark themes behave unchanged.
* No visual regressions were observed.

fix(editor): cardinal direction arrows with label are invisible in exported SVG
items.body:
Fixes #11439. Originally reported in obsidian-excalidraw-plugin#1454.

## Problem

When an arrow with a bound text label is exported to SVG, the arrow line disappears and only the label remains — but only when the arrow is perfectly horizontal or vertical. Angled arrows export correctly, making the issue appear intermittent.

## Root cause

The gap behind an arrow label is rendered using an SVG `<mask>` in `packages/excalidraw/renderer/staticSvgScene.ts`.

The mask was created without explicitly setting `maskUnits`, causing it to use the SVG default of `objectBoundingBox`. For perfectly horizontal or vertical arrows, the geometric bounding box collapses along one dimension, causing the computed mask region to collapse as well and fully clip the arrow. The label itself is rendered outside the mask and therefore remains visible.

## Fix

Create the mask with `maskUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` and explicit dimensions so the mask region no longer depends on the arrow's geometric bounding box.

This preserves existing behavior for diagonal arrows while fixing the previously broken axis-aligned case.

## Testing

- Added a regression test in `packages/excalidraw/tests/scene/export.test.ts`.
- Exports a horizontal labeled arrow and asserts the gap-mask is pinned to a non-degenerate `userSpaceOnUse` region (jsdom does not rasterize SVG, so visual masking cannot be observed directly).
- Confirmed the new test fails on `master` and passes with this change.
- `yarn test:typecheck`, ESLint, and existing export test suites pass.

cc @dwelle. Thanks @zsviczian for the earlier investigation and debugging pointers on the linked issue.

items.title: feat(editor): allow for dragging bound text along an arrow's path
items.body:
# Summary

Arrow labels can be dragged along their arrow. A label's place is stored on the text element as `labelPosition`, a normalized arc-length parameter (0–1) over the arrow's whole path, and the label's x/y is derived from it. Because the parameter covers the whole path rather than one segment, the label keeps its place when points are dragged, when midpoints are inserted or removed, and when the arrow is resized. (An earlier iteration anchored labels to a segment; that approach is gone.)

Closes #9338.

## Behavior

- With an arrow selected, hovering its label shows a grab cursor and dragging moves the label along the path, to the point closest to the pointer. Works on straight, curved and elbow arrows; dragging past an end clamps to that end.
- Point handles and the segment midpoint knob keep precedence over a label sitting on top of them, so a labeled arrow can still be bent at its middle and its points dragged. Hover runs the same hit tests in the same precedence as pointer down, so the cursor never promises an interaction a click won't deliver. Known trade-off: at common zooms a very short label can be entirely covered by the midpoint knob's radius.
- The label is only grabbable where it is the topmost thing under the pointer; an element stacked above the arrow wins.
- New labels start at the middle (0.5). Binding text to an arrow sets 0.5; unbinding clears it.
- Double-clicking a labeled arrow, or clicking it with the text tool, edits the existing label where it currently sits, not at the arrow's midpoint.
- Elbow arrows position the label along their logical (unrounded) polyline.
- Releasing a label drag never rebinds the arrow's endpoints.
- SVG export now cuts the same padded hole around the label as the canvas and PNG export do; they had disagreed by 5px per side since arrow labels were introduced.

## Data model

`ExcalidrawTextElement.labelPosition?: number | null`. Every text element now carries it at construction (`null` unless it is an arrow label), and restore normalizes it (clamped to 0–1, `null` when missing or invalid). Older clients preserve the field through restore.

## Implementation notes

- `LinearElementEditor.getPointAtPathParameter` maps the parameter to a point using per-arrow path metrics (segment lengths and prefix sums) cached on the element version; `handleBoundTextDragging` does the inverse with a closest-parameter search per segment.
- The derived label position is memoized per text element, keyed on the arrow's and the text's versions, since it is needed on every hit test, bounds query and render. On 200 labeled curved arrows a pointer move dropped from 1.4ms to 0.37ms.
- Whether a pointer-down grabbed the label is kept on `pointerDownState`, so it is scoped to the gesture by construction.
- Math additions: `curveClosestParameter` (with `curveClosestPoint` built on it), `lineSegmentClosestParameter`, `lineSegmentPointAt`, and `curvePointAtLength` accepting an already-known length.
- Hover affordances are refreshed when a gesture ends, so the resting cursor is correct without moving the mouse.
- An attempt to keep arrowheads visible outside the label hole was reverted as not worth the two-pass rendering; keeping labels from being dragged over an arrowhead is left for a follow-up.

## Tests

- The path parameter survives midpoint insertion; elbow arrows use the logical path.
- Label drag: grabs when a covering element is below the arrow and not when it is above; an elbow route point under the label; midpoint precedence, including under a covered label.
- Hover and pointer-down agree on a handle under the label; grabbing a handle just beyond the arrow's tip keeps the selection instead of starting a box selection.
- Resize keeps `labelPosition` and the label on the path midpoint; SVG and canvas cut the same label hole.

## Notes

The curve hit-test offset on rotated arrows found while testing edge cases is tracked in #10948.
